# How does a single gene behave?

**The question:** take one interesting gene — how different is it between biofilm and
planktonic? The plot that answers it: a **boxplot with the data points shown**.

## Setup {-}

```{r setup05, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
data_dir <- c("data", "../data", "project/data", "../project/data")
data_dir <- data_dir[dir.exists(data_dir)][1]
counts <- read_tsv(file.path(data_dir, "gene_counts.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
meta   <- read_tsv(file.path(data_dir, "metadata.tsv"),    show_col_types = FALSE)
de     <- read_tsv(file.path(data_dir, "DE_biofilm_vs_planktonic_24h.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

# tidy counts (built in the 'compare my samples' chapter) — we need it again here
counts_long <- counts %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(gene_id, gene_name), names_to = "sample", values_to = "count") %>%
  left_join(meta, by = "sample")
```

Let's pick the gene that changed the most (we'll meet the full result in the next
chapter):

```{r}
top_gene <- de %>%
  filter(padj < 0.05) %>%
  slice_max(abs(log2FoldChange), n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  pull(gene_id)

top_gene
```

Plot its expression at 24 h, one box per lifestyle, with every replicate shown on top:

```{r}
counts_long %>%
  filter(gene_id == top_gene, timepoint == "24h") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = lifestyle, y = log10(count + 1), colour = lifestyle)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 2) +
  labs(title = top_gene, x = NULL, y = "log10(count + 1)")
```

<div class="important">
  <strong>⭐ Important:</strong> always show the actual data points on top of a boxplot —
  with only a few replicates, the box alone can hide the real story.
</div>

## ...and over the time course {-}

The boxplot showed one timepoint. A **line plot** shows how the gene changes across the
whole experiment (5 h → 10 h → 24 h). We average the replicates in each group:

```{r}
counts_long %>%
  filter(gene_id == top_gene) %>%
  mutate(timepoint = factor(timepoint, levels = c("5h", "10h", "24h"))) %>%
  group_by(lifestyle, timepoint) %>%
  summarise(mean_expr = mean(log10(count + 1)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = timepoint, y = mean_expr, colour = lifestyle, group = lifestyle)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(title = top_gene, x = NULL, y = "mean log10(count + 1)")
```

<div class="tip">
  <strong>💡 Tip:</strong> timepoints are text (<code>"5h"</code>, <code>"10h"</code>,
  <code>"24h"</code>), which ggplot would sort alphabetically. We make them an ordered
  <code>factor</code> so the x-axis runs 5 h → 10 h → 24 h, and set
  <code>group = lifestyle</code> so each lifestyle gets its own line.
</div>

### 👉 Your turn {-}

Pick a different gene (any `gene_id` from the `de` table) and plot it the same way.
Does it go up or down in biofilm?

<details>
<summary>Solution</summary>
```{r, eval=FALSE}
my_gene <- "SAUSA300_RS00670"   # change me

counts_long %>%
  filter(gene_id == my_gene, timepoint == "24h") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = lifestyle, y = log10(count + 1), colour = lifestyle)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 2) +
  labs(title = my_gene)
```
</details>
